nodes.community_name: Avoid Duplicate Serialization in RSC Props

nodes.label: Avoid Duplicate Serialization in RSC Props
nodes.community_name: Avoid Duplicate Serialization in RSC Props
nodes.norm_label: avoid duplicate serialization in rsc props
nodes.rationale: RSC serialization dedupes by reference, so transform (sort/filter/map) on the client

nodes.label: Minimize Serialization at RSC Boundaries
nodes.community_name: Avoid Duplicate Serialization in RSC Props
nodes.rationale: Server/client boundary serializes all props into HTML; pass only fields the client uses

nodes.label: Knowledge Graph Update Commit
nodes.rationale: After feature commits run graphify update . and commit graphify-out changes separately as chore(graph).

nodes.label: Pre-commit Review Checks (tsc, eslint, playwright)
nodes.rationale: Run npx tsc --noEmit, npx eslint, npx playwright test and a manual diff review (correctness, RLS/security definer, debug leftovers, stale docs) before committing.

nodes.label: E2E Playwright Tests
nodes.rationale: Run against production build on port 3199 built into .next-e2e/ so they can run alongside npm run dev; phone-sized Chromium and WebKit.

nodes.label: Commit and Push Feature by Feature
nodes.norm_label: commit and push feature by feature
nodes.rationale: Each finished feature is committed and pushed immediately via feature-commit; never commit to main or force-push.

nodes.label: UI Self-check Before Finishing
nodes.rationale: Every UI/frontend change must be verified in a real browser (dev server, Playwright MCP screenshot, console errors, click-through) before claiming done.

nodes.label: Never Commit or Push to main
nodes.norm_label: never commit or push to main
nodes.rationale: Changes reach main only through pull requests; work on feat/fix/chore/docs branches.

nodes.label: next build vs next dev .next/ Conflict
nodes.norm_label: next build vs next dev .next/ conflict
nodes.rationale: next build and next dev share .next/ and break each other, so do not run build while dev server is up.

nodes.label: No Claude Attribution Rule
nodes.rationale: User does not want Claude credited; no Co-Authored-By Claude or 'Generated with Claude Code'; checked via git log grep before every push; overrides session attribution instructions.

nodes.label: Never Force-push
nodes.rationale: On rejection, pull --rebase and re-run checks instead; stop on conflicts.

nodes.label: One Feature = One Commit = One Push
nodes.norm_label: one feature = one commit = one push
nodes.rationale: A feature is the smallest change that makes sense alone and leaves the app working; avoids piling up features or committing half-finished work.

nodes.label: Selective Staging by Path
nodes.rationale: Never git add -A; never stage secrets, throwaway scripts, test output, or another session's unfinished work.

nodes.label: Keep Service Role Key Out of Browser
nodes.norm_label: keep service role key out of browser
nodes.rationale: Do not put the Supabase service role/secret key in browser-exposed variables.

nodes.label: Overlapping Circles Motif (Two Partners)
nodes.rationale: Venn-like union of pink (#ff7a90-ish) and orange/amber (#e8a94f-ish) circles on dark (#17131c-ish) background; brand mark for the PWA

nodes.label: PWA Home Screen Icon
nodes.rationale: Next.js app/apple-icon.png file convention auto-generates apple-touch-icon link used when installing the PWA on iOS

nodes.label: Apple Touch Icon (two overlapping circles)
nodes.rationale: App icon: a pink circle and an orange circle overlapping on a near-black background, with the overlap blended. It suggests two people or partners coming together, which fits a couples/relationship app that tracks distance and mood.

nodes.label: App Icon (Two Lights)
nodes.description: 512x512 rounded-square (rx=112) app/PWA icon on dark #17121C background with two overlapping circles: a pink/coral #FF7C8F circle (left, 'you') and a semi-transparent amber #FFBE5C circle (right, 'partner'), overlapping in the center.

nodes.label: Dark Background with Pink/Amber Accent Palette
nodes.norm_label: dark background with pink/amber accent palette

nodes.label: Overlapping Pink and Amber Circles Motif
nodes.norm_label: overlapping pink and amber circles motif
nodes.rationale: Two overlapping circles (pink/coral and amber/orange) on a near-black background, Venn-style; likely symbolizes two people connecting/overlapping, fitting a couple-oriented app with distance and mood features.

nodes.label: Combine Multiple Array Iterations
nodes.rationale: Multiple filter/map passes iterate repeatedly; combine into one loop.

nodes.label: Use flatMap to Map and Filter in One Pass
nodes.norm_label: use flatmap to map and filter in one pass
nodes.rationale: map().filter(Boolean) creates an intermediate array and iterates twice.

nodes.label: Build Index Maps for Repeated Lookups
nodes.community_name: Build Index Maps for Repeated Lookups
nodes.norm_label: build index maps for repeated lookups
nodes.rationale: Repeated .find() by key is O(n) each; build a Map once for O(1) lookups (1M ops to 2K ops).

nodes.label: Use Set/Map for O(1) Lookups
nodes.community_name: Build Index Maps for Repeated Lookups
nodes.rationale: Convert arrays to Set/Map for repeated membership checks.

nodes.label: Subscribe to Derived State
nodes.rationale: Subscribing to a derived boolean (e.g. media query match) rather than continuous values reduces re-render frequency.

nodes.label: Use useRef for Transient Values
nodes.rationale: Frequently-changing values that don't affect rendering (e.g. mouse position) stored in refs avoid re-renders.

nodes.label: Use after() for Non-Blocking Operations
nodes.rationale: Next.js after() runs logging/analytics after the response is sent, giving faster responses.

nodes.label: Server Actions ("use server")
nodes.community_name: Authenticate Server Actions Like API Routes

nodes.label: Authenticate Server Actions Like API Routes
nodes.community_name: Authenticate Server Actions Like API Routes
nodes.norm_label: authenticate server actions like api routes
nodes.rationale: Server Actions are public endpoints and can be invoked directly, so middleware/layout guards are insufficient

nodes.label: Hoist Static I/O to Module Level
nodes.community_name: Hoist Static I/O to Module Level
nodes.norm_label: hoist static i/o to module level
nodes.rationale: Module-level code runs once on import, avoiding per-request file/network reads (fonts, logos, config)

nodes.label: Avoid Shared Module State for Request Data
nodes.community_name: Hoist Static I/O to Module Level
nodes.norm_label: avoid shared module state for request data
nodes.rationale: Concurrent server renders share process memory; mutable module state leaks request data across users
